_meta.methodology: Assets mapped are physical facilities materially relevant to frontier or large-scale AI compute. Announced capacity is separated from operational capacity. Unknown values are left blank rather than estimated. Sources ranked: primary > institutional > specialist industry > major reporting.

assets.name: ASML EUV Production — Veldhoven
assets.technology: EUV lithography systems (NXE, NXE:3800E, High-NA EUV)
assets.role: Sole commercial producer of EUV lithography systems required for sub-3nm chip manufacturing. No commercial alternative exists.
assets.current_capacity: 60+ EUV systems/year (guidance: raising 30% annually for 2 years)
assets.policy_exposure: Dutch export licensing controls EUV exports. Zero EUV systems shipped to China. US-Dutch allied control alignment. High-NA EUV ($400M/unit) not yet in volume production.
assets.time_to_relief: No substitution visible. ASML itself is supply-constrained, raising capacity 30%/yr to meet demand.

timeline.note: Ongoing production. Capacity raising 30%/yr.

assets.name: Carl Zeiss SMT — EUV Optics
assets.technology: EUV optics and optical systems for ASML EUV machines
assets.role: Sole supplier of EUV optical systems integrated into every ASML EUV machine. The optics chokepoint within the chokepoint.
assets.policy_exposure: German export control jurisdiction. Key node in US-NL-DE allied equipment coalition.

timeline.note: Long-operational. Sole EUV optics supplier.

assets.name: TSMC Fab 18 — Tainan
assets.technology: 3nm (N3E/N3P), 2nm (N2) — leading-edge logic
assets.role: TSMC's primary advanced-node logic fab complex. Produces majority of frontier AI accelerators including Nvidia Blackwell/Vera Rubin, Apple M-series, AMD Zen 5. 3nm hit 28% of TSMC wafer revenue in Q4 2025.
assets.current_capacity: ~90,000–100,000 wafers/month at 2nm across Taiwan facilities (early 2026 estimate)
assets.policy_exposure: Taiwan contingency risk. No direct export control jurisdiction over TSMC — but TSMC relies on ASML EUV (Dutch controls), US EDA software (BIS jurisdiction), and US semiconductor equipment (BIS).
assets.time_to_relief: 2nm fully booked into 2028 per TSMC investor briefings. No near-term capacity relief for new customers.

timeline.note: 3nm operational 2022, 2nm Q4 2025. Booked into 2028.

assets.name: TSMC CoWoS Advanced Packaging — Taiwan
assets.technology: CoWoS-S, CoWoS-L (advanced AI chip packaging integrating GPU + HBM)
assets.role: Primary advanced packaging for AI accelerators. Integrates GPU die with HBM stack. Currently the binding constraint in AI hardware supply per Epoch AI and industry analysts. Nvidia holds estimated ~60% of CoWoS-S/L capacity.
assets.current_capacity: ~1M wafers demand in 2026 (Silicon Analysts June 2026, sell-side estimate — treat as directional); CoWoS-S $750/chip, CoWoS-L $1,100/chip
assets.policy_exposure: Taiwan concentration risk. CoWoS expansion partly in US (Arizona) but minimal volume before 2028.
dependencies_upstream: Ajinomoto ABF substrate film (dominant market position)
assets.time_to_relief: Lead time 50–78 weeks (Silicon Analysts June 2026, directional). TSMC expanding: marginal relief late 2026, meaningful 2027–28 as new CoWoS lines qualify. Demand also expanding.

timeline.note: Binding now. Meaningful relief 2027-28 as new lines qualify.

assets.name: TSMC Fab 21 — Phoenix, Arizona
assets.technology: 4nm (Phase 1, in production), 3nm/2nm (Phase 2, targeted H2 2027)
assets.role: TSMC's first US advanced-logic fab. Phase 1 (4nm) in volume production since 2025. Phase 2 (3nm/2nm) is primary US reshoring of leading-edge foundry capacity. Total US commitment $265B.
assets.policy_exposure: Primary beneficiary of CHIPS Act funding. US domestic supply chain initiative. Advanced-node qualification with major customers still required for Phase 2.
dependencies_downstream: Nvidia, AMD, other Phase 2 customers (qualification ongoing)
assets.time_to_relief: Phase 1 (4nm): operational. Phase 2 (3nm/2nm): H2 2027 earliest, full qualification 12–18 months after. Arizona estimated <5% of Taiwan advanced-node capacity before 2028 (denominator: advanced-node wafer starts — exact figure not publicly disclosed).
assets.source_title: TSMC investor briefings 2026 + CHIPS Act filings

timeline.note: Phase 1 (4nm) operational 2025. Phase 2 (2nm) H2 2027, full qual 2028.

assets.name: SK Hynix M15 — Cheongju (HBM)
assets.technology: HBM3E, HBM4 — high-bandwidth memory for AI accelerators
assets.role: SK Hynix's primary HBM production facility. SK Hynix holds estimated ~53% of global HBM market and supplies approximately two-thirds of Nvidia's HBM4. Entire 2026 HBM output allocated under non-cancellable contracts.
assets.current_capacity: HBM4 yield: ~80% as of August 2026 (Silicon Analysts; directional estimate)
assets.policy_exposure: South Korea export control alignment with US/allies. BIS controls on HBM exports to China are a critical part of export control architecture — Korean cooperation essential.
dependencies_upstream: ASML EUV (for HBM production — $7B+ order placed)
Samsung/SMIC alternative packaging (none credible at scale)
assets.time_to_relief: 2026 sold out. 2027 already booked. SK Hynix CEO: 2027 will be worst supply shortage in memory industry history. Meaningful new capacity: 2028+ from M15X/Y2 expansion.
assets.source_title: SK Hynix Q1 2026 earnings + CEO public statement

timeline.note: Operational. 2026 fully allocated. Relief only from M15X expansion.

assets.name: SK Hynix M15X — Cheongju (New HBM)
assets.technology: HBM4, HBM4E — next-generation HBM expansion
assets.role: Major capacity expansion for HBM. Part of SK Hynix's +54 trillion KRW (~$39B) investment across Y2 and M17 fabs. Primary future relief for HBM supply constraint.
assets.timeline_volume_production: Initial production February 2027 (Y1 phase); full ramp 12–18 months after
assets.policy_exposure: Same as M15. BIS HBM export control cooperation essential.
assets.time_to_relief: Initial production Feb 2027 → full ramp 2028. M17 expansion: Dec 2028. Y2: Jun 2029. Constraint material relief: 2028–2029.
assets.source_title: SK Hynix Q1 2026 earnings + capex announcements

timeline.note: Initial production Feb 2027. Full ramp 2028. M17: Dec 2028. Y2: Jun 2029.

assets.name: Samsung Semiconductor — Pyeongtaek P3 (HBM/Logic)
assets.technology: HBM3E, HBM4 (memory); SF2/SF3 (logic foundry)
assets.role: Samsung's flagship fab complex. HBM4 yield improved from <60% at Feb 2026 launch to ~80% by August 2026 (Silicon Analysts; directional). Priced ~30% below SK Hynix to win H20 and B200 supply slots.
assets.policy_exposure: South Korea — allied with US. Foundry arm competes with TSMC for AI chip customers.
assets.time_to_relief: HBM: ramping through 2026–27. Foundry: 2nm (SF2) qualification ongoing; limited external capacity.
assets.source_title: Samsung semiconductor investor relations + Silicon Analysts August 2026

timeline.note: HBM4 ramping. Yield improved to ~80% by Aug 2026. Meaningful volume 2027.

assets.name: Micron Technology — Boise, Idaho (HBM)
assets.technology: HBM3E, HBM4 — AI memory
assets.role: US-based HBM producer. Grown from 2% HBM market share (2023) to approximately 11% (2025–26). Began shipping HBM4 for Nvidia Vera Rubin in early 2026. Provides US domestic HBM supply — strategically significant for export control architecture.
assets.announced_capacity: $3.87B advanced packaging plant announced in Indiana (SK Hynix partnership noted separately)
assets.policy_exposure: US company — directly subject to BIS export controls. Provides US domestic alternative to Korean HBM. CHIPS Act recipient.
assets.time_to_relief: Ramping. Meaningful additional capacity from new Idaho fabs: 2027–2028.
assets.source_title: Micron investor relations + Q2 FY2026 earnings

timeline.note: HBM4 shipping for Vera Rubin early 2026. New Idaho capacity 2027-28.

assets.name: Applied Materials — Santa Clara (Equipment)
assets.technology: CVD, PVD, ALD deposition; CMP; epitaxy; metrology
assets.role: World's largest semiconductor equipment company by revenue. Deposition and materials engineering equipment is required at every leading-edge node. Subject to BIS export controls — Applied Materials sales to China require licenses for advanced-node equipment.
assets.policy_exposure: US company. BIS export controls apply to advanced-node equipment. US-origin technology triggers FPDP jurisdiction. Critical node in US-NL-JP allied equipment control coalition.

timeline.note: Long-operational equipment company.

assets.name: Lam Research — Fremont, California (Equipment)
assets.technology: Etch (plasma, DRIE); thin film deposition (ALD, CVD); cleaning
assets.role: Dominant etch and deposition equipment supplier. Etch steps multiply at advanced nodes — Lam's equipment is required at every leading-edge fab. BIS export controls cover Lam equipment for advanced-node applications in China.
assets.policy_exposure: US company. BIS jurisdiction. Advanced packaging revenue outlook raised from >40% to >70% YoY growth (current fiscal year).
assets.source_title: Lam Research investor relations + FY2026 guidance

timeline.note: Long-operational equipment company.

assets.name: KLA Corporation — Milpitas, California (Inspection)
assets.technology: Process control, inspection, and metrology for semiconductor manufacturing
assets.role: Dominant inspection and metrology equipment supplier. Detects defects at atomic scales — required at every advanced-node fab. No chip production at leading-edge nodes is viable without process control at KLA's capability level.
assets.policy_exposure: US company. BIS export controls apply. US-origin equipment triggering FPDP reach.

timeline.note: Long-operational equipment company.

assets.name: Tokyo Electron — Tokyo (Equipment)
assets.technology: Coater/developer, CVD, etch, cleaning equipment for semiconductor fabs
assets.role: Japan's largest semiconductor equipment company and globally essential supplier. TEL's coater/developer systems are required for lithography process steps at every advanced fab. Part of the US-NL-JP equipment coalition — Japan's October 2023 export controls covering 23 equipment categories were essential to closing circumvention gaps.
assets.policy_exposure: Japanese export control jurisdiction (October 2023 — 23 equipment categories). Essential node in allied control coalition. US-Japan coordination extends effective BIS reach through Japanese equipment controls.
assets.source_title: Tokyo Electron investor relations + Japan METI export controls October 2023

timeline.note: Long-operational. Japan export controls Oct 2023.

assets.name: Japan Materials — EUV Photoresists (TOK, JSR, Shin-Etsu)
assets.technology: EUV photoresists, silicon wafers, EUV mask blanks (AGC/Hoya), specialty chemicals
assets.role: Japan controls >90% of EUV photoresists (TOK, JSR, Shin-Etsu) and ~51% of global silicon wafers (Shin-Etsu, SUMCO). AGC and Hoya hold a 93% duopoly on EUV mask blanks. These materials cannot be substituted on short timelines — they are as much a chokepoint as the equipment itself, but receive less policy attention.
assets.policy_exposure: Japanese export control jurisdiction. Japan's materials controls complement Dutch/US equipment controls. China's domestic photoresist industry is making progress at mature nodes but not yet at EUV-grade.

timeline.note: Long-operational materials cluster.

assets.name: Synopsys — Sunnyvale (EDA Software)
assets.technology: EDA software — chip design tools, verification, process design kits
assets.role: One of two dominant EDA software companies (with Cadence). US EDA firms control >90% of the market for advanced chip design software. Switching EDA tools requires years of re-tooling — the switching cost is itself a chokepoint. BIS export controls on EDA for advanced-node chip design in China are in effect.
assets.policy_exposure: US company. BIS EDA export controls. US jurisdiction over EDA software provides a non-physical chokepoint that applies wherever EDA is used — including by chip designers outside the US who design chips later manufactured at controlled foundries.
assets.source_title: Synopsys investor relations + BIS Federal Register

timeline.note: Software — no physical timeline.

assets.name: Nvidia — Santa Clara (Accelerator Design)
assets.technology: AI accelerator design — Blackwell (B200), Vera Rubin (2026), Rubin Ultra (2027)
assets.role: Dominant AI GPU designer. Nvidia designs but does not manufacture chips — manufacturing at TSMC, packaging at TSMC CoWoS, memory from SK Hynix/Micron/Samsung. Holds estimated ~60% of TSMC CoWoS capacity in 2026. Vera Rubin entered full production May 2026.
assets.policy_exposure: H200 exports to China subject to BIS case-by-case licensing (Jan 2026). H20 previously approved for China. Vera Rubin (more advanced) not approved for China. $500B announced US AI infrastructure investment.
dependencies_upstream: TSMC logic (sole foundry for leading AI GPUs)
assets.source_title: Nvidia Q1 FY2027 earnings + Nvidia Newsroom May 2026

timeline.note: Design company. Vera Rubin in production May 2026.

assets.name: ChangXin Memory (CXMT) — Hefei
assets.technology: DRAM; targeting HBM3 commercial yields 2026
assets.role: China's primary domestic DRAM and HBM development effort. Targeting HBM3 commercial yields in 2026. Currently 2–3 generations behind SK Hynix frontier (HBM4/4E at ~80% yield). Progress is real but not yet demonstrated at commercial scale.
assets.policy_exposure: Subject to US export controls on HBM and advanced DRAM. BIS entity-list status restricts equipment supply. China domestic memory effort — strategic priority for Beijing.
assets.time_to_relief: HBM3 yields by end-2026 possible but unconfirmed at commercial scale. 2–3 generation gap to current SK Hynix frontier (HBM4). Commercial supply of China-domestic HBM at meaningful scale: 2027–2028 at earliest.

timeline.note: HBM3 yields targeted end-2026. Commercial scale uncertain. 2-3 gen behind frontier.

assets.name: SMIC — Shanghai (Advanced Foundry)
assets.technology: 7nm via DUV multi-patterning; older nodes at scale
assets.role: China's most advanced chip foundry. Produces 7nm chips using DUV multi-patterning — technically viable but at higher cost and likely lower yield than EUV-based production. Manufactures Huawei Ascend AI accelerators. Cannot access EUV lithography (Dutch/US controls holding).
assets.policy_exposure: On BIS Entity List. Restricted access to advanced equipment and EUV. DUV multi-patterning is SMIC's workaround — produces 7nm but cannot economically reach sub-3nm without EUV.
dependencies_upstream: Domestic equipment alternatives (NAURA, AMEC — progress at mature nodes)
assets.time_to_relief: For China: SMIC represents domestic partial substitution. Cannot match TSMC economics at frontier nodes without EUV access.
assets.source_title: SMIC investor relations + BIS Entity List

timeline.note: 7nm via DUV operational. No EUV access. Not a near-term relief for China.

assets.name: Intel Fab — Hillsboro, Oregon (18A)
assets.technology: Intel 18A (1.8nm-class) — backside power, RibbonFET gate-all-around
assets.role: Intel's leading-edge process for external foundry customers. Intel 18A is in risk production 2026. Represents the most credible alternative to TSMC for advanced-node external foundry work — but not yet in high-volume manufacturing for AI accelerators. AMD announced split of some 2nm orders to Samsung, not Intel, in May 2026.
assets.policy_exposure: CHIPS Act primary recipient. US domestic advanced foundry — strategic objective. Key question: can Intel achieve competitive yields at 18A for external AI accelerator customers?
assets.time_to_relief: High-volume manufacturing at 18A for external customers: 2027+ depending on yield progress. Intel foundry previously missed multiple node timelines — confidence is moderate.

timeline.note: 18A risk production 2026. HVM for external customers 2027+. Yield progress uncertain.

assets.name: Microsoft Data Center — Ames, Iowa
assets.technology: Large-scale AI training and inference cluster
assets.role: Representative of US hyperscaler AI data center expansion. Microsoft has committed $80B+ in data center investment in FY2025 alone. Iowa and other Midwest locations chosen partly for power availability and land cost.
assets.policy_exposure: US infrastructure. Power availability is primary constraint — grid interconnection timelines and transformer procurement.

timeline.note: Operational data center cluster.

assets.name: Google / DeepMind AI Infrastructure — US (Multiple)
assets.city: Multiple (Mayes County OK, Lenoir NC, etc.)
assets.technology: TPU v5/v6 clusters, AI training infrastructure
assets.role: Google operates some of the largest AI training clusters globally using custom TPUs (manufactured at TSMC). $75B+ data center capex committed for 2025. Google designs its own AI accelerators — reducing dependence on Nvidia but not on TSMC foundry or HBM supply.
assets.policy_exposure: US infrastructure. Google's TPU design capability is a strategic asset but foundry dependence on TSMC remains.

timeline.note: Operational. $75B+ capex 2025.

assets.name: MGX / G42 AI Infrastructure — Abu Dhabi
assets.technology: Large-scale AI data center and compute infrastructure
assets.role: UAE sovereign wealth-backed AI compute buildout. Microsoft partnership with G42 for AI infrastructure. UAE becoming a significant AI compute geography — partly enabled by energy availability and government investment. Geopolitically significant: US scrutiny of UAE AI chip access due to China ties.
assets.policy_exposure: US export controls on Nvidia chips to UAE subject to end-use monitoring. UAE-China technology ties are a US policy concern. UAE's AI ambitions require sustained access to advanced chips.

timeline.note: Operational. US export control conditions apply.

assets.name: US Grid Transformer Constraint
assets.company: Multiple (Siemens, ABB, Hitachi Energy, SPX Transformer)
assets.technology: High-voltage power transformers for data center grid interconnection
assets.role: Grid transformers are the binding infrastructure constraint for new US data center connections. Lead times of 1–2+ years have become a primary bottleneck for new AI data center capacity. Unlike chip fabs, transformer capacity does not respond to capital on short timelines. CSIS has explicitly identified grid infrastructure as a binding AI deployment constraint.
assets.policy_exposure: US domestic infrastructure. Limited by manufacturing capacity (primarily US plants of Siemens, ABB, Hitachi Energy), steel supply, and skilled labor — not export controls.
dependencies_downstream: All new large-scale AI data center construction in US
assets.time_to_relief: Lead times 1–2+ years. New manufacturing capacity: multi-year permitting and construction. Policy-responsive but not on short timelines.

timeline.note: Lead times 1-2+ years. New capacity multi-year. Policy-dependent.

assets.name: Northern Virginia Data Center Corridor — Power Constraint
assets.technology: Grid interconnection constraints for world's largest data center cluster
assets.role: Northern Virginia hosts the world's largest concentration of data centers. Grid interconnection queues have become multi-year — new data center projects face 3–7 year waits for grid connections in some cases. This is the clearest current example of power becoming a binding AI deployment constraint. Not a chip problem — a grid problem.
assets.policy_exposure: US regulatory/permitting constraints. Dominion Energy territory. State-level permitting reform underway. Not responsive to federal chip policy.
assets.time_to_relief: Interconnection queue reform: policy-dependent, 2–5 year timeline. New transmission: 5–10 years. Nuclear/gas behind-the-meter: 2–5 years depending on project.
assets.source_title: CSIS Wadhwani Center 'Powering Innovation' 2026 + Dominion Energy filings

timeline.note: Interconnection queue 3-7+ years. Reform underway but slow.

assets.name: Amazon Web Services — AI Infrastructure (US)
assets.technology: Trainium/Inferentia custom AI chips + Nvidia clusters
assets.role: AWS operates the largest cloud AI infrastructure globally. Amazon committed $100B+ in data center capex for 2025. AWS Trainium is a custom AI chip (TSMC-manufactured) reducing Nvidia dependence — but still HBM and CoWoS dependent.
assets.policy_exposure: US infrastructure. Government cloud contracts (GovCloud). Power constraint is primary deployment bottleneck.

timeline.note: Operational. $100B+ capex 2025.

assets.name: Arm Holdings — Cambridge (CPU/AI Architecture)
assets.technology: CPU/NPU architecture IP licensed to virtually all chip designers
assets.role: Arm's architecture underpins virtually all mobile chips and an increasing share of data-center processors (AWS Graviton, Apple M-series, Nvidia Grace CPU). Not a physical manufacturing chokepoint — an IP licensing chokepoint. Arm is subject to US jurisdiction (listed on Nasdaq; SoftBank-controlled). BIS controls could theoretically extend to Arm architecture licenses to Chinese companies.
assets.policy_exposure: UK company, Nasdaq-listed, SoftBank-controlled. US jurisdiction through listing and customer relationships. RISC-V is the primary alternative architecture being adopted in China to reduce Arm dependence.

timeline.note: IP licensing — no physical capacity timeline.

assets.name: SK Hynix Advanced Packaging — West Lafayette, Indiana
assets.technology: HBM advanced packaging for AI accelerators
assets.role: SK Hynix's US advanced packaging facility — $3.87B investment. Represents US reshoring of HBM packaging capacity. In proximity to Purdue University semiconductor research cluster.
assets.policy_exposure: CHIPS Act incentive. US-Korea cooperation on strategic semiconductor manufacturing.

timeline.note: Production targeted 2028. CHIPS Act recipient.

assets.name: TSMC Fab — Kumamoto, Japan (JASM)
assets.company: TSMC (JASM joint venture with Sony, Denso, Toyota)
assets.technology: 12/16nm, 22/28nm — not leading-edge but strategically important for automotive/IoT
assets.role: TSMC's Japan joint venture. Phase 1 (12nm) in production 2024. Phase 2 (6nm) construction underway. Not advanced enough for frontier AI accelerators — relevant for automotive, IoT, and supporting Japan's semiconductor ecosystem rebuilding. Sony, Denso, Toyota as JV partners.
assets.policy_exposure: Japanese government subsidy. Part of Japan's semiconductor independence strategy. JASM strengthens US-Japan-Taiwan semiconductor cooperation.

timeline.note: Phase 1 (12nm) operational 2024. Phase 2 (6nm) 2027.

assets.name: Broadcom — Palo Alto (AI ASIC Design)
assets.technology: Custom AI ASICs (Google TPU, Meta MTIA, others); networking silicon
assets.role: Broadcom is the leading custom AI ASIC designer — a significant and growing alternative to Nvidia GPUs for hyperscaler inference. Broadcom AI ASIC revenue exceeded $20B in FY2025. Custom ASICs reduce per-unit GPU dependence but still require TSMC CoWoS and HBM.
assets.policy_exposure: US company. ASICs produced at TSMC — CoWoS and HBM dependent. Less export-control exposure than Nvidia (ASICs are customer-specific, not off-the-shelf).

timeline.note: Design company. ASIC revenue $20B+ FY2025.

assets.name: TSMC Fab — Dresden, Germany (ESMC)
assets.company: TSMC (ESMC joint venture with Infineon, NXP, Bosch)
assets.technology: 28/22nm — mature nodes for automotive and industrial
assets.role: European semiconductor manufacturing initiative. Mature nodes (28/22nm) — not relevant for frontier AI accelerators but important for European automotive and industrial chip supply independence. EU Chips Act strategic investment.
assets.policy_exposure: EU Chips Act funding. European semiconductor sovereignty initiative. Germany strategic industrial policy.
assets.source_title: ESMC corporate + EU Chips Act filings

timeline.note: 28/22nm. Production targeted 2027. Not relevant for frontier AI.

assets.name: Samsung Semiconductor — Taylor, Texas
assets.technology: 4nm / 2nm — advanced foundry for external customers
assets.role: Samsung's US advanced foundry expansion. Phase 1 (4nm) construction; timeline has slipped. Intended to provide a TSMC alternative for US-based chip designers. Primary target: advanced AI and mobile chips. Samsung Foundry has lost customers in recent years due to yield challenges.
assets.policy_exposure: CHIPS Act recipient. US domestic foundry alternative to TSMC. Progress slower than announced — confidence moderate.
assets.time_to_relief: Delayed. Production timeline uncertain — Samsung Foundry has faced yield and customer-retention challenges. Conservative estimate: 2027 at earliest for meaningful volume.

timeline.note: Delayed. 4nm construction. Timeline uncertain — moderate confidence.

assets.name: Huawei — Shenzhen (Ascend AI Accelerator)
assets.technology: Ascend 910B/910C AI accelerators; designed internally, manufactured at SMIC
assets.role: China's primary domestic AI accelerator. Manufactured at SMIC using DUV multi-patterning (7nm-class). Viable for many inference workloads. CUDA software moat remains the largest barrier to broad Ascend adoption. Volume is constrained by SMIC yield at advanced nodes.
assets.policy_exposure: Huawei on BIS Entity List. Primary target of US semiconductor export controls. Huawei's ability to access advanced chips from external foundries is blocked — reliant on SMIC for advanced nodes.

timeline.note: Ascend 910B/C in production. SMIC-dependent. Volume constrained.

assets.name: US Nuclear Restart / AI Power Supply
assets.city: Multiple (Three Mile Island PA, Comanche Peak TX, etc.)
assets.technology: Nuclear power for AI data center baseload supply
assets.role: Nuclear power restarts and new SMR projects are emerging as the preferred solution for AI data center baseload power — 24/7 carbon-free supply without intermittency. Microsoft restarted Three Mile Island Unit 1 (contracted with Constellation). Amazon, Google, and others pursuing nuclear PPAs. This represents the energy-policy dimension of AI industrial policy.
assets.policy_exposure: NRC licensing jurisdiction. State-level permitting. IRA tax credits. Nuclear restart is faster than new build — but still 2–5 year process for new sites.
assets.time_to_relief: Constellation TMI restart: operational 2024. New SMRs: 2030+. Nuclear PPAs: 2026–2030 depending on project.

timeline.note: TMI restart operational 2024. New SMRs 2030+. Nuclear PPAs 2026-2030.
